title: 2 Core concepts
body:
2 Core concepts
A few core ideas explain the whole plugin.

Transcripts: how a page becomes text
A page of handwriting is an image. To search it, quote it, or discuss it, it has to become text. That is what READ does,
and every page goes through the same two steps:
STEP 1 · OCR

STEP 2 · VISION

Mistral OCR 4 reads the page

Ministral 14B reads the image

Fast, cheap and powerful. It returns the text plus a

With the OCR text riding along as a hint. Vision

confidence score for each word, but it doesn't “see”

understands layout, tables, drawings, margin notes

drawings, schemas or handwritten notes on a PDF,

and your own conventions, and it follows the prompt

and takes no instructions.

you can edit (§3.3).

Each result is stored on the tablet with a fingerprint of the page. This allows every change to be easily identified and
only modified pages are re-read. The fingerprint follows the content, not the location: rename a note or PDF, move it
to another folder, or move or copy a page between two notes, and its transcript is found again, never recharged. A rename takes everything with it, the file's sync mode, the agents that know it, and any lock you set.
Page after page, those transcripts become a library: your own local, searchable copy of what you wrote. It powers
Search (one query across every notebook, in seconds) and Export. Nothing is uploaded to build it, it lives in the
plugin's private storage, on the device only.

One AI provider, by choice: Mistral
SmartNote AI talks to exactly one provider, Mistral AI, a European company under the GDPR. That is a deliberate,
privacy-first decision, not a limitation: your notes stay under European law, and on a paid plan Mistral never trains on
your data. The full reasoning, and what it means if you write from outside the EU, is in §6.2.

FREE TIER

Every feature works on the free tier, with comfortable limits: all models are available, and field-testing in July
2026 gave roughly ~1300 transcribed pages / month plus a lot of chat before reaching the limits. Only a paid
plan guarantees Mistral never trains on your data.
Mistral currently offer 10€/months of API usage to anyone subscribing to Pay-as-you-go. Check Mistral billing
rules. With 10€ budget you can transcribe ~3000 pages.

Chat and agents
Once a page has a transcript (or on demand, live), you can chat about it. The floating assistant is a movable panel that
sits over your note. It always knows what you are looking at, and you can add anything else: other pages, whole
notebooks, a lassoed image.
An agent is the same chat with a memory of its own: a name, a persona, a model, and a set of library documents it
always knows. Four ready-made agents ship with the plugin and can be added in one tap:

title: Partner app and attach to a bug report at
body:
Partner app and attach to a bug report at
github.com/AgP42/SN-PluginSmartNoteAI/issues. The file already carries the plugin
version, your device model, the Android build and a
summary of your library, so there is nothing else to look up.
It records the plugin's own activity only, never the text of
your pages, your questions, the AI's answers, or your API
key. The names of the notes and folders it touched do
appear in clear, it is a plain text file, so you can open it and
edit those names out before sending if you would rather
not share them. A crash writes the log by itself, with the
error, before the plugin goes down, so exporting after a
restart still shows what happened.
Appearance. Text size (S/M/L/XL) and Button size apply
everywhere, floating panel included, set these first if the UI
feels small. Note toolbar side tells the plugin where your
pen toolbar sits, so panels never cover it.

3.3 · Configuration Door 2: READ: AI transcript params
This door shapes what the AI is told when it reads a page. It drives the Vision step.

Fig. 3.2, Prompt blocks.

Fig. 3.3, Glossary & helpers.

The prompt is not hidden: it is a list of editable blocks, joined into the instruction actually sent. The shipped blocks are
a tested, high-performing base, but they are tuned to my notes: to get good results on yours, you must adapt them
to your own context, the language(s) you write in, your names, acronyms and jargon (the Glossary), your financial
and unit conventions, and how you use drawings and templates. Every block has a Reset, plus a Reset to default, all
this page at the top, so you can experiment freely.

Glossary (your

The single biggest quality lever: your names, acronyms and jargon.

Three helpers sit under the glossary: Suggest words from my library mines what has already been read for frequent

Mistral Small, Medium and Large all can.

3.4 · Configuration Door 3: CHAT & AGENTS: your assistants
One page for every assistant. CHAT is the default; its persona, model, answer style and quick actions apply
everywhere unless an agent overrides them. Up to 8 custom agents plus CHAT (9 entries in all).

Fig. 3.4, Agents & model.

Fig. 3.5, Web & answer style.

Fig. 3.6, Quick actions.

Fig. 3.7, Documents & cost.

Model. Any Mistral model name works; presets are the ones that can use the chat's Web and have Vision
capability (needed for the Lasso feature). Each preset points to -latest, so a new Mistral model is used
automatically when available. The screen shows each model's real price and description, so pick from what it
displays rather than a fixed ranking, prices and capabilities change.

title: Web search is one-shot: you arm it in the chat panel and it applies to your next
body:
Web search is one-shot: you arm it in the chat panel and it applies to your next message only. Web answers cite
their sources (~0.01 € per search).
Answer style. Precise sticks to the facts, Creative allows looser phrasing, Balanced is the model's own tuning.
Persona (system prompt). Who the assistant is and how it talks to you, prepended to every conversation.
Quick actions are the one-tap prompts under the chat input. Toggle, reorder, edit or add your own; they write into
the input field so you can adapt before sending. Lasso quick actions (up to 3) appear only while a lassoed image
is in context.
+ Add preset. Adds a ready-made agent to the list, the quickest way to start; edit it from there or build your own
from scratch.
Context documents & cost. Build an agent's context from the Library. Folders and whole notes stay live (future
pages included automatically); specific pages are fixed. The screen tells you how many pages are already read,
what reading the rest would cost, and the token weight, less context is cheaper. Within a conversation only the
first message pays the full context; caching then bills the rest at about 10%.

The Library is your local transcript store and the
cockpit for syncing, searching and exporting. The tree

4.1 · Synchronisation
Every folder and note carries a mode chip, set with one tap. Setting a chip costs nothing, it only saves a preference. A
folder's mode covers everything under it; a single document can override its folder. A row that follows its parent shows
an inherited chip, ↳ Sync: X (the mode it takes from above); tapping cycles Off → Manual → Auto → inherit when a
parent folder is tracked, so you can always fall back to the folder's choice.

A good habit: active notebooks on Auto, archives on Manual, anything private on Off.

Notes and PDFs have different constraints
A page is rendered by the app that owns it: note pages need the note app in the background; PDF Vision needs the
document reader.
The OCR step of a PDF is the exception, it reads the file's bytes whatever is on screen. The plugin probes what it
can render at every pass (Rendering via: note app / PDF reader / none yet). If PDF Vision pages wait and rendering
fails, a ▶ Resume PDF Vision button appears, you decide when to tap it; the plugin never opens a document by itself.

title: HONEST LIMITS
body:
HONEST LIMITS
Auto works while the plugin lives. Close
everything and it pauses, then resumes where
it stopped.
In the background, how long the system keeps it
running is out of the plugin's hands.
Nothing runs while the device is off.
A page takes roughly 8-30 s (render + OCR +
Vision). A first full-notebook sync is a “start it and
let it run” job.
Unsupervised, Auto reads at most 500 pages per
session; actions you ask for yourself (Sync now,
Force sync, Force Vision) have no such cap.

Fig. 4.2, The Synchronisation frame.

4.2 · Browse transcripts

Fig. 4.3, Pages as tiles.

Fig. 4.4, One page, three views.

Open a document to see every page as a tile: the first lines of its transcript, its source, or not read yet. A page read
and found empty says (blank page), it is done, not pending. Open a page and you get three things side by side: the
transcript, the original page image, and the Supernote's own live OCR (free, for comparison)[only for .note].
From here you can: edit the transcript by hand (you can lock it afterwards to avoid the page to be overwritten); tap
an underlined “unsure” word to fix just that word; Redo AI transcript to re-read the page (a single unified OCR +
Vision pass); Rotate right + redo or Rotate left + redo to re-read a page rotated 90° (rarely needed, landscape
pages are usually straightened automatically); and Export this page or add it to the chat.

title: Lock a page or a document
body:
Lock a page or a document
A lock freezes a transcript you are happy with. Lock a single page from its page view, or a whole document from the
page grid, whose chip then reads

🔒 Lock document (N p. locked); locked rows also show a 🔒 in the Library. A

locked page is never re-read automatically, even if its ink changes later, so a page you have hand-corrected stays

exactly as you left it. On a locked page the Redo AI transcript and Rotate right / left + redo buttons are greyed out
and decline; the lock/unlock toggle and Edit stay available, so manual corrections are always allowed.
The lock survives sync and Restore backup, and it blocks every Clear: a locked document refuses its own Clear, and
locked pages survive a document Clear, Clear transcripts of Off notes and Clear ALL transcripts alike. The
confirmation message spells out what will be kept.

title: 4.3 · Search
body:
4.3 · Search
Search runs over your local transcripts only, what has already
been read. A document never synced is invisible until you sync
it. Results are capped, and the line under the field always
shows how your query was understood. On each result line you
can open the transcript, Go to page (the Supernote opens the
real page), or add the page to the chat. A document set to Off
shows an Off chip instead of the add button: its pages are
never sent to the AI.
Fig. 4.5, Search.

YOU TYPE

title: 5 The floating assistant
body:
5 The floating assistant
Open the assistant gives you a movable, resizable
panel that floats over your note: you keep writing on
the page while you talk about it.
Drag the header to move it, the black bar at the bottom to
resize, the ▣ button to collapse it into a floating bubble, ⤢ to
snap it to a corner or full screen, and ✕ to close it.

Fig. 5.1, The floating panel.

5.1 · CHAT
The brain dropdown (name + arrow in the header) switches between CHAT and your agents. It shows the current
model, how many documents and pages are loaded, New chat, and your History.
Quick actions under the input write a prompt into the field; you send it yourself with the M (Mistral logo) button.
Web is one-shot: arm it and it applies to the next message only. Web answers cite their sources.
A Stop button is always available while the assistant works.
Reading pages not read yet starts right away; only a large batch (more than 100 pages ~0,4€) asks you to confirm the
price first. Below that, the read begins directly and its cost shows in the Library's MANUAL panel. Off files ask for a onetime consent, and their text is stored nowhere.
Follow-up questions cost about 10% of the first, thanks to prompt caching.

5.2 · Agents
Pick an agent from the brain dropdown when you start a
conversation. It brings its persona, model, answer style, quick
actions and its documents. You can also change agent midconversation to change the chat's behaviour, the full history is
sent to the new model, so the discussion continues.

Fig. 5.2, The brain dropdown.

5.5 · Lasso
Select part of a page with the Supernote lasso and tap Ask SmartNote AI. The selection is attached to the

title: 6.2 · Why Mistral only
body:
6.2 · Why Mistral only
Why Mistral, and why Mistral only? That is a deliberate choice, here is the reasoning.
Our handwritten notes are usually very personal data, and privacy was my key concern throughout this plugin's
development. The question is not only “is the model smart?” but “under whose laws does this text land, and who
can compel access to it?”
The plugin already keeps exposure small: everything stays on the tablet, each request is transient (no memory beyond
a short-lived cache), and Off files are never sent. But the biggest privacy factor is the choice of AI provider.

Mistral · EU (France)

Other jurisdictions

Under EU law (GDPR), Mistral must limit use of

In the US, the CLOUD Act lets authorities compel a

and heavy fines. Protection by law, not by a toggle.

Intelligence Law (Art. 7) and the Data Security Law

Data is processed on EU servers, under EU
jurisdiction, so no foreign authority can quietly

require companies to cooperate with the state on
request. A training opt-out only helps as far as you

compel access. GDPR also demands transparency

trust it is honoured. And these powers reach data

about what is kept and for how long, and any

provider is meant to close.

You are in the US or China? An EU model may help you too: your notes get European-grade handling and sit outside
your own country's easiest reach. No provider hides you from a determined state, and nothing dangerous should go
into any cloud, but for everyday notes, moving them under EU law is a real privacy gain wherever you live.
Is the quality there? For reading handwritten notes or PDFs and chatting about them, no need for the latest state-ofthe-art, overly expensive model. Mistral's OCR4 and Ministral vision models are very strong on reading (chosen on
measured results), while Mistral Small, Medium and Large are also very good for discussion, summary, content
understanding, basic calculation and everyday tasks. Important for good results: clear prompts, readable handwriting
and your own glossary well filled in (see configuration door 2).
Top providers are clearly ahead in raw capability, but I am convinced that Mistral is “good enough” for Supernote user
needs, and that trade-off is made on purpose, driven by privacy first.
